newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper mine halted for fifth day.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper mine halted for fifth day.

text.p: Production was halted at the strike-hit Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal on Friday despite a brief resumption of work by some employees on Thursday afternoon, company officials said.
"The situation is still the same. There is no work going on," said one company official contacted by Reuters at the mine, 250 km southeast of Lisbon.
Somincor, the state-owned company that manages the mine, said that production had partially resumed on Thursday afternoon when busloads of striking miners abandoned picket lines to travel to Lisbon.
The miners, who are protesting company plans for Sunday working, went to lobby Somincor headquarters in the capital and the Economy Ministry.
A spokeswoman for the company told Reuters that around half the afternoon shift had entered the mine to work and that output was running at near 80 percent.
But union leaders who had travelled to Lisbon were sceptical about the numbers and said that the pickets would be back outside the mine earlier on Friday.
The company says that the 107,000 tonne per year mine needs to work seven days a week in order to boost efficiency.
